newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw seen expanding after unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw seen expanding after unit sale.

text.p: Laidlaw Inc, which today agreed to sell its solid waste unit to Allied Waste Industries Inc for US$1.65 billion, is expected to use part of the proceeds on acquisitions, analysts said on Wednesday.
"I think it's an extremely attractive deal," said Griffiths McBurney analyst Greg Misztela.
Richardson Greenshields of Canada analyst Dunnery Best said a possible Laidlaw target was American Medical Response Inc, which would complement Laidlaw's ambulance service business.
Laidlaw earlier this year swallowed the transportation division of Scott's Hospitality Inc, consolidating its position as North America's largest school bus unit.

Best said that "ironically, American Medical Response shares were weaker today due to a Wall Street Journal article reporting on heavy insider trading." Shares in the ambulance firm fell 2-1/2 to 33-7/8 in moderate trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
But Misztela said Laidlaw would more likely concentrate on smaller companies.
"American Medical Response is a relatively large company right now and a little bit bigger than Laidlaw's operations. There's several smaller operations that they could go after," Misztela said.
"I think they're going to be using the cash prudently," Misztela said.

Best added that "in recent years, (Laidlaw) has managed to maintain an excellent record of growth through acquisition as it refocused on two main areas: transport, with ambulances and school buses, and toxic waste handling."

American Medical Response chief executive Howard Siegel said his company was not in talks with Laidlaw, but he did not rule out future negotiations. "I think there's some synergism," he said in a telephone interview.
Best said that Laidlaw was still rated a buy, with a target price of 18 within a year.

Laidlaw topped actives on the Toronto Stock Exchange with its class B shares up 1.30 to 15.60 on 8.1 million shares in late afternoon trading. The stock is trading at its highest since 1991, Best said.

Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday that it revised Laidlaw's outlook to stable from negative. It also affirmed its ratings on the company's senior unsecured debt and corporate credit ratings at triple-B'-plus. Moody's said it affirmed Laidlaw's senior debt rating at BAA2.
Laidlaw chief executive James Bullock said in an interview that the firm could make more acquisitions, saying: "We have capacity for opportunities that will come along."
Bullock added that he did not exclude buying out Laidlaw's majority shareholder, Canadian Pacific Ltd, which holds a 47.2 percent voting stake.
